en.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island after Guards target Bahrain, White House withdraws FDA nominee
en.dek: US military strikes missile site on Qeshm Island in retaliation for Iranian targeting of US assets; White House withdraws Heidi Overton FDA nomination
facts: US military struck a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island on 2026-11-17 in retaliation for Iranian targeting of US personnel and assets in Bahrain
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeted US personnel and assets in Bahrain prior to the US strikes
White House withdrew Heidi Overton's nomination for FDA commissioner on 2026-11-18, one day before scheduled Senate committee vote
Asif Merchant was sentenced to 330 months in prison for plotting to assassinate President Donald Trump at Iran's behest in 2024
Secretary of State Marco Rubio downplayed reports of an Iranian dirty bomb threat to Washington following intelligence reports of Iranian plans to target senior Trump administration officials
body: On 2026-11-17, the US military struck a missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a US military official.
The strike came in retaliation for Iranian targeting of US personnel and assets in Bahrain, the military said.
Iran's state media reported that US forces attacked Qeshm Island, describing it as the latest exchange of strikes between the two nations.
The Strait of Hormuz, a key route for oil and gas shipments, has become the focus of the stalemated Middle East war, the US military said.
On 2026-11-18, the White House withdrew the nomination of Heidi Overton for FDA commissioner, a White House official confirmed.
The withdrawal occurred one day before a scheduled Senate committee vote, according to CNN and Fox News.
Asif Merchant was sentenced to 330 months in prison for plotting to assassinate President Donald Trump at Iran's behest in 2024, according to Times of India and The Hindu.
Prosecutors stated the plot was in retaliation for Washington's killing of an Iranian military commander in 2020, both outlets reported.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio downplayed reports of an Iranian dirty bomb threat to Washington, seeking to reassure Americans following intelligence reports of Iranian plans to target senior Trump administration officials.
Rubio also condemned intelligence leaks regarding the threat, according to The Jerusalem Post.
en.context: Tensions between the US and Iran have escalated following Iranian targeting of US personnel and assets in Bahrain, prompting US strikes on Iranian territory. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical chokepoint for global energy supplies. The White House withdrawal of an FDA nominee reflects internal administration decisions unrelated to the military escalation.
